record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a topological group that is countable, Fréchet-Urysohn, and non-metrizable?

evidence.quote:
Every ﬁrst-countable space X is Fr´ echet-Urysohn, that is, a point x ∈ X is in
the closure of a subset A of X only if some sequence in A converges to x.

Problem 8 (V. I. Malykhin, < 1980). Construct in ZF C a non-metrizable countable
Fr´ echet-Urysohn topological group.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is Fréchet–Urysohn if for every subset $A\subseteq X$ and every point $x\in\overline{A}$ there exists a sequence $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $A$ converging to $x$. A topological group is a group $G$ equipped with a topology making the multiplication $G\times G\to G$ and inversion $G\to G$ continuous. The group $G$ is countable if its underlying set is countably infinite, and metrizable if its topology is induced by some metric.

Decide, working only in ZFC (i.e., without additional set-theoretic axioms), whether there exists a countable, Fréchet–Urysohn, non-metrizable topological group. Equivalently, construct such a group in ZFC or prove that no such construction is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: Malykhin's problem was resolved by M. Hrušák and U. A. Ramos-García, who constructed a model of ZFC in which every countable Fréchet–Urysohn topological group is metrizable. Since such groups also exist under various set-theoretic hypotheses (e.g., MA), the existence statement is independent of ZFC; hence no ZFC construction is possible.

status_evidence.title: Malykhin's problem
status_evidence.snippet: Hrušák and Ramos-García construct a model of ZFC where every separable Fréchet topological group is metrizable, thereby solving Malykhin's 1978 problem.
status_evidence.claim: Independence of the existence of a countable non-metrizable Fréchet–Urysohn group from ZFC; no ZFC construction exists.

status_evidence.title: Malykhin's problem - ScienceDirect (Advances in Mathematics)
status_evidence.snippet: Published paper by Hrušák and Ramos-García resolving Malykhin's problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is settled: it is consistent with ZFC that no countable non-metrizable Fréchet–Urysohn group exists.
